title: Compliance Memorandum: Liability Notices and Patient Charges on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
Compliance memorandum on advance notices of financial liability and on the patient charge types of the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

## 1. When a notice is needed

1.1 *Retired clause.* As originally written, this memorandum provided, for every supply, that when an item or quantity the customer wants is expected not to be paid by the payer (above the tier's allowance without supporting documentation, an item the tier does not cover, or a replacement before the payer's replacement interval), Larkfield supplies it billable to the customer only after the customer signs the tier's liability notice for that item and quantity before the ship date. That unqualified wording is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, which treats one case separately: a supply on the CGM Original Medicare Program whose advance-notice units are counted by the rule for Medicare advance beneficiary notices is supplied billable to the customer, for the counted units, only after the customer signs the advance notice for the item and those units before the ship date. Every other supply, including a commercial-tier supply covered by a plan member waiver, continues on exactly the terms just quoted.

1.2 *Retired clause.* As originally written, this memorandum provided that the customer signs the notice personally, and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them. That wording is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis for a Medicare advance beneficiary notice counted by the rule for such notices, under which the customer signs it personally through their own signing step on the enrollment and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them. Every other notice continues on exactly the terms just quoted: the customer signs it personally, and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them.

## 2. The notice by tier

2.1 On the CGM Original Medicare Program the notice is the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (form CMS-R-131); the claim is still submitted to Medicare with the notice on file, and the customer becomes liable only for a line Medicare denies.

2.2 On the CGM Medicare Advantage Program no notice can make the member liable; the member becomes liable only for an item for which the plan has issued a pre-service organization determination denial, recorded as a prior authorization denial for that item.

2.3 On the CGM Self-Pay Program no notice applies, because every item is priced at the Larkfield cash price.

## 3. Patient charge types

A patient charge is posted only as one of these charge types:

| Charge type | Posted for |
|---|---|
| Self-pay price | A self-pay refill at the cash price |
| Standard shipping | A self-pay shipment below the free-shipping threshold |
| Expedited shipping | A customer-requested expedite |
| Non-covered item | An item or quantity covered by a signed liability notice, or by a Medicare Advantage organization determination denial, that the payer denied, charged at the Larkfield cash price of the units concerned |

A non-covered item charge requires a liability notice signed on or before the ship date covering that item and at least those units, or on the CGM Medicare Advantage Program the plan's organization determination denial for that item; without it the amount is Larkfield's write-off and is never billed to the customer.

## 4. Points of judgement (hypothetical)

- A notice signed for 2 units supports a non-covered item charge for up to 2 units of that item; it does not support a non-covered item charge for 3 units, because the notice must cover at least the units charged.
- A notice signed the day after the ship date does not support a non-covered item charge for that shipment; one signed on the ship date does.
